_comment: DATED, STATIC pricing ballpark for v1. Deterministic — the LLM must never invent these. Figures are rough on-demand approximations for a general-purpose vCPU+RAM service and per-GB internet egress; refresh periodically and update _as_of. NOT a quote.

_units.compute: USD per vCPU-hour and USD per GB-RAM-hour

_egress_comment: Egress is NOT one price — it's a tier ladder by WHERE the bytes cross. We price the locality tier (same-region / cross-region / cross-cloud+internet) as a LOW-HIGH RANGE because region-pair rates vary. Per-GB, USD, DIRECTIONAL list prices as of _as_of; excludes free-tier allowances, committed-use/negotiated discounts, and NAT/load-balancer processing fees. Not a quote. Keys: internet rate stays per-provider (differs most); same-region & cross-region tiers are broadly consistent across AWS/GCP/Azure so we use one shared range.

same_region.note: Same region: free within an AZ over private IP; ~$0.01/GB each way if it crosses AZs.

cross_region_same_cloud.note: Inter-region within one cloud: most pairs ~$0.01-0.02/GB; a few source regions/continent pairs run higher.

cross_cloud.note: Leaving the cloud to another provider or the public internet: the expensive tier; GCP Premium ~$0.12, AWS ~$0.09, Azure ~$0.087 at entry bands.

_egress_sources: AWS/GCP/Azure published data-transfer pricing pages + corroborating 2026 guides (usage.ai, nops.io, egresscost.com, redresscompliance, bacancy, tatacommunications). Rounded to ranges; verify against the provider pricing page for a specific region pair.
_source: Compute coefficients for [aws+azure+gcp] derived from Vantage live data using ONE matched method: general-purpose 4GB/vCPU families (AWS m5/m6i, GCP n2-standard, Azure D-series v5), on-demand Linux, mean $/vCPU across regions, 25% split to RAM. Egress remains static. Apples-to-apples DIRECTIONAL comparison, not a quote.

_serverless_usd._comment: On-demand list prices for request-driven serverless compute, before free tiers and discounts. DIRECTIONAL, not a quote. Azure Functions prices are not bundled (the public page renders prices client-side and could not be verified).

aws.product: AWS Lambda (event functions, x86, first tier)
